sections.h2: What are my choices for selling a house in Cedar Park?
sections.html:
A Cedar Park owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or sell to a cash buyer who takes the house as it stands. Each route trades time, repair work and certainty differently, so the right one depends on the condition of the house and how soon you need to close.

  • List with an agent: best when the house is in good shape and you can wait through showings, buyer financing and appraisal.
  • Sell it yourself: you keep the agent's share of the work and the cost, but you handle pricing, disclosures, contracts and the title company yourself.
  • Cash buyer, as-is: suits houses with deferred repairs, tenants, probate paperwork or a foreclosure clock running. Closing can be quick, and the buyer does not need a lender's appraisal.

Whichever route you pick, the same Cedar Park facts apply: which appraisal district holds your parcel, what the city requires for permits and rentals, and how the deed gets recorded.

sections.h2: How did Cedar Park become the city it is today?
sections.html:
Cedar Park grew from a ranch settlement into a suburb of Austin that was incorporated as a city in 1973. The Texas Historical Commission marker in front of the public library tells the story: in 1873 a couple bought a large tract rich in cedar and limestone, a post office opened in 1874 under the name Running Brushy, and the railroad arrived in 1882 when the name changed to Bruggerhoff. Five years later the present name was adopted.

The same marker says the founder opened a cedar yard to sell fence posts as barbed wire spread, that little growth came in the first half of the twentieth century, and that by 1960 nearly all traces of the old community had disappeared. Growth in Austin during the 1970s pulled people north, and the city incorporated in 1973. The city's economic development group now describes Cedar Park as the third largest city in the Austin metro and as part of Williamson County.

sections.h2: Which appraisal district and county handle my Cedar Park property taxes?
sections.html:
Look at your latest tax statement: it names the county and the appraisal district that carry the parcel. The Williamson Central Appraisal District covers Williamson County addresses, and the city's own economic development page places Cedar Park in Williamson County.

Texas has no state property tax. Local units set the rates, and the appraisal district values each property as of January 1. A lien for that year's taxes attaches on January 1 as well, which is why the tax bill matters at closing even when you sell in the middle of the year. Bills go out around October 1. Taxes unpaid on February 1 are delinquent, and the collector then adds a six percent penalty plus one percent interest, per the Texas Comptroller.

Never rely on a rate quoted in a listing or an online calculator. Ask the Williamson County tax office for the current adopted rates for each unit that taxes your address, and ask the title company how it will prorate the year's bill between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: How do the homestead exemption and the 10 percent cap work in Cedar Park?
sections.html:
A homeowner who lives in the house can claim a residence homestead exemption, and the appraisal district limits how fast the assessed value of that home can rise. The Williamson CAD explains that a home qualifies for the cap in the second full year the exemption has been on the property for the same owner, and that the cap holds yearly increases in existing assessed value to 10 percent no matter how fast market value climbs.

The same page says the cap does not transfer with ownership. A buyer starts fresh and may see a bigger jump in assessed value than you did, which is worth knowing if you advertise your tax bill. The appraisal district also notes the following:

  • You apply once and the exemption stays, unless you move or add another exemption such as over 65 or disabled.
  • A Texas driver license or ID with your current address is required.
  • Processing can take up to 90 days.
  • The chief appraiser reviews each homestead exemption at least once every five tax years.

On the state side, school districts must give a $140,000 homestead exemption, and owners 65 or older or disabled get an extra $60,000 from the school district and a school tax ceiling, according to the Comptroller. Local units may add more.

sections.h2: What does Cedar Park's short-term rental registration mean for sellers?
sections.html:
If your Cedar Park house is rented for stays of 30 consecutive days or fewer, it falls under a registration rule that City Council adopted in April 2026. Registration became required on October 1, 2026, costs $100 a year, and is paired with Hotel Occupancy Tax reporting under Chapter 10 of the City Code. The city estimates about 200 active short-term rentals.

A buyer who plans to run the house as a rental will ask whether a registration exists, whether hotel tax was remitted and whether the account is current. Registered owners use an online portal to watch tax remittance, and the city lists Development Services at 512-401-5100 for registration questions and Utility Billing at 512-401-5300 for tax payments. If you rented the house this way, gather the registration confirmation and tax records before you list it, so the buyer's questions do not stall the contract.

sections.h2: What permit and repair rules should I check before selling in Cedar Park?
sections.html:
Open permits and unfinished work are the usual reason a buyer's inspector or title company pauses a Cedar Park closing. The city runs permits through the MGO Connect portal, and Development Services sits at the City Hall campus at 450 Cypress Creek Road, Building 1.

If a permit was opened for a deck, a roof, a water heater or a remodel and never finished, ask Development Services for a status check. The city asks for an email request to reopen or cancel a permit and then reviews it, so start early. Sellers who do not want to deal with that can sell as-is to a buyer who agrees to take the house with the open item.

sections.h2: How are the deed and the closing handled in Cedar Park?
sections.html: A deed to a Williamson County house is recorded with the county clerk, and a Texas instrument that conveys land has to be signed and acknowledged before a notary or another authorized officer before it can be recorded. Per the State's county clerk manual, recording starts at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, with extra clerk fees on top.

sections.h2: What if the Cedar Park house is inherited, in foreclosure or has a tenant?
sections.html:
Those three situations each have a state clock, and each one favors starting early. The Texas State Law Library describes the rules in plain language.

  • Foreclosure: a borrower can reinstate by paying the past-due amount within 20 days of the notice of default. The notice of sale has to go out at least 21 days before the sale, and sales happen at the courthouse on the first Tuesday of a month between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m.
  • Inherited house: a will can be probated within 4 years of death. A muniment of title lets heirs move the property without full administration when debts other than liens are absent, and a small estate affidavit is limited to estates of $75,000 or less, not counting homestead and exempt property.
  • Tenant in place: a landlord usually needs to give at least 3 days' written notice to vacate before filing for eviction in justice court, unless the lease sets a different period.

A cash buyer can buy a house with a tenant or an open probate matter, but the title company still has to see clear authority to sell. A Williamson County probate lawyer can say which paper applies.

sections.h2: What should I do first if I want to sell my Cedar Park house quickly?
sections.html:
Start with five checks, in this order, and you will know your real options within a few days.

  • Pull your latest tax statement and confirm the appraisal district and any unpaid balance.
  • Ask Development Services whether any permit on the address is open or expired.
  • Collect the loan payoff figure, or confirm the house is free of a mortgage.
  • If the house is a short-term rental, assemble the registration and hotel tax records.
  • Decide whether you need to close by a fixed date, such as a foreclosure sale date or a move.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Cedar Park house with an open building permit?
faqs.a: Yes, but the permit complicates the sale. Residential permits in Cedar Park expire if no work starts, or if work stops, for 180 days. Ask Development Services at 512-401-5100 to review the status, or sell as-is to a buyer who accepts the open item.

faqs.q: Do I need to register my Cedar Park short-term rental before selling?
faqs.a: If the house has been rented for 30 days or fewer at a time, registration became required on October 1, 2026 at $100 a year. Buyers who want to keep renting will ask for the registration and your hotel occupancy tax records.

faqs.q: Does my homestead tax cap pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The Williamson Central Appraisal District states that the homestead cap does not transfer with ownership. The new owner applies for their own exemption, and the cap starts counting from their first full year.

faqs.q: When are Texas property taxes delinquent, and what is added?
faqs.a: Taxes unpaid after January 31 are delinquent on February 1. The collector then adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest, according to the Texas Comptroller. Ask the Williamson County tax office for your exact balance.

faqs.q: How is a foreclosure sale scheduled in Texas?
faqs.a: A foreclosure sale is held at the courthouse on the first Tuesday of the month, between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. The lender must send notice at least 21 days ahead. A borrower may reinstate within 20 days of the notice of default.
